    Describe a table without hiding what is missing

    Source: R/describe.R
    sdt_describe.Rd

    A descriptive table over a sdt_participants register, a sdt_course_composition table, or any data frame. Every variable reports its counts, its missingness and the summary its type deserves – counts and percents for a categorical variable, mean, SD, median, IQR and range for a numeric one – optionally split by a grouping column.

    Usage

    sdt_describe(
  x,
  by = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  na_report = c("row", "column", "footnote"),
  digits = 2
)

# S3 method for class 'sdt_describe'
format(x, ..., max_groups = 8L, max_levels = 12L)

# S3 method for class 'sdt_describe'
print(x, ..., max_groups = 8L, max_levels = 12L)

    Arguments

    x

    A sdt_participants object, a sdt_course_composition object, or any data frame.

    by

    Optional single column name to split by. NULL, the default, pools every row. Rows whose grouping value is missing form their own group rather than disappearing.

    vars

    Optional character vector of columns to describe. Defaults to a curated set for the two classes this package produces, and to every non-indicator column otherwise.

    na_report

    Where to surface missingness: "row", "column" or "footnote". It cannot be switched off.

    digits

    Decimal places for the printed statistics. Percentages use one fewer, since a percent already carries two significant figures more than the proportion it comes from. The returned tibble is never rounded.

    max_groups

    Groups to print before the rest are summarised in one line. The object keeps every group either way.

    max_levels

    Levels to print per categorical variable.

    Value

    A sdt_describe object: a tibble::tibble() subclass with one row per group, variable and level. Two families of counts share every row and are named apart so they cannot be confused. n, n_level_observed and n_level_imputed belong to the row – to one level of one categorical variable, or to the values of one numeric variable. n_observed, n_imputed, n_missing, n_valid and n_records belong to the variable, and are repeated on each of its rows, so that n_observed + n_imputed + n_missing == n_records holds on every row of the table. The three percents, pct_missing and the numeric statistics complete it. tibble::as_tibble() returns it bare; sdt_describe_render() returns the display-ready shape.

    Every percent states its denominator

    A categorical level carries three shares, and all three are in the returned tibble whatever the report style:

    • pct_observed – over answered rows only. Its denominator excludes both missing rows and filled ones.

    • pct_valid – over rows that carry a value. Its denominator excludes missing rows and includes filled ones.

    • pct_total – over every row in the group. Its denominator includes everything, missing rows included.

    pct_valid and pct_total are the two a reader usually means by "the percent", and they differ exactly when something is missing. pct_observed differs from pct_valid exactly when something was imputed.

    Missingness cannot be switched off

    na_report decides where missingness is surfaced, never whether it is:

    • "row" – each categorical variable gains a (missing) row, and each numeric variable a missing line of its own.

    • "column" – the missing count and percent appear beside every row.

    • "footnote" – they are collected under each block, complete variables named as such so silence is never ambiguous.

    n_missing and pct_missing are columns of the returned tibble in all three cases.

    Imputed values are flagged, not absorbed

    Where the input carries indicators – .missing_<field> and .imputed_<field> from sdt_read_participants(), <covariate>_missing and n_<covariate> from sdt_course_composition() – each row is placed in exactly one of three states: observed, imputed or missing. Imputed rows are counted separately, never as observations, and numeric variables carry mean_observed, sd_observed and median_observed alongside the all-values statistics so both are visible at once.

    For a variable with a fill rule, n_imputed + n_missing is the number of rows nobody answered: some of them were filled and some were not, and the two are reported apart rather than added up for the reader. That is why title_level reports no missing values and 99 imputed ones on the TDSC register – an empty title box is filled with none, and the fill is visible in every share it touches.

    A value that is present in a row whose own missing indicator is set is not an observation. It is counted as imputed when an imputation indicator or a zero denominator (n_<covariate> of 0) says it was filled, and as missing otherwise. That zero-denominator rule is what catches sdt_course_composition(impute = "median"), which fills without flagging: the fill is reported as imputed anyway, and named as unflagged.

    Level, not group

    The participant register has no group column, so a composition descriptive split by course is a between-course description with as many points as there are courses. There is no split by group to be had.

    See also

    sdt_describe_participants() for the participant defaults, sdt_participant_summary() for the participant-only summary this generalises, sdt_course_composition() for the imputing half of the policy.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(
  grade = c("consultant", "resident", "consultant", NA),
  years = c(11, 2, 7, NA),
  .missing_grade = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),
  .imputed_grade = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
)
sdt_describe(d, vars = c("grade", "years"))
#> <sdt_describe> 2 variables over 4 records
#> Denominators: val% excludes missing, all% includes it; obs% excludes fills too.
#> Missingness: reported as its own row, and never suppressed.
#> 
#>   grade                      n     imp    val%    all%
#>     consultant               2       0    66.7    50.0
#>     resident                 1       0    33.3    25.0
#>     (missing)                1       -       -    25.0
#>   years
#>     n 3   imputed 0
#>     missing 1 of 4 (25.0%)
#>     mean 6.67 (SD 4.51)   median 7.00 [4.50, 9.00]
#>     range 2.00 to 11.00
tibble::as_tibble(sdt_describe(d, vars = "grade"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 28
#>   group variable type   level missing_row     n n_level_observed n_level_imputed
#>   <chr> <chr>    <chr>  <chr> <lgl>       <int>            <int>           <int>
#> 1 (all) grade    categ… cons… FALSE           2                2               0
#> 2 (all) grade    categ… resi… FALSE           1                1               0
#> 3 (all) grade    categ… (mis… TRUE            1                0               0
#> # ℹ 20 more variables: n_observed <int>, n_imputed <int>, n_missing <int>,
#> #   n_valid <int>, n_records <int>, pct_observed <dbl>, pct_valid <dbl>,
#> #   pct_total <dbl>, pct_missing <dbl>, mean <dbl>, sd <dbl>, median <dbl>,
#> #   q25 <dbl>, q75 <dbl>, iqr <dbl>, min <dbl>, max <dbl>, mean_observed <dbl>,
#> #   sd_observed <dbl>, median_observed <dbl>
